html:
SMTO-FIL-0042 — The Gateway lost track of this file copy

GUID: f8da2187-a129-4fd9-a22c-0849a72889ea
Slug: file-transfer-session-unavailable
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • Partway through a copy between Gateways, the Gateway no longer had the copy open, for example because it restarted or the copy sat idle too long. SMTO can't tell from this alone whether the file was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and use Check connection on both Gateways. A Gateway that restarted or disconnected mid-copy forgets the copies it had open.
  3. Only if the file is missing or different, ask SMTO to copy it again. Copying again without checking could replace a file that was already saved.

What success looks like

  • The destination file matches the original, or a new copy finishes and is verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the destination Gateway. If you can't tell whether the file arrived, don't repeat the copy until they have checked it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway had no live transfer session for the run/transfer key (closed, expired after 300 s idle, or lost on Gateway restart), the journal had no record to update, or journal begin found an existing record for the key.

What this means

  • The requested active transfer session is absent, a required durable record cannot be found, or journal begin finds an existing record for the identity. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The requested active transfer session is absent, a required durable record cannot be found, or journal begin finds an existing record for the identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original run/transfer identity, durable status and any destination publication before starting another session.

How to fix it

  • Use destination_status or destination_reconcile for the transfer_id on the destination Gateway to learn whether the stage was committed, and check the Gateway log for restarts or idle expiry. Settle the original transfer (abort or verify) before starting a new copy; never replay destination_commit.
  • Recover or reconcile the original transfer state before creating a new session.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original transfer is settled and any supported new work uses a valid owned session.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
